cohort: The participants were women who underwent spontaneous labor and vaginally delivered cephalic singleton fetuses with normal neonatal outcomes at the Taipei Chang Gung Memorial Hospital in Taiwan during two periods: 1991-1995 (n=10,721) and 2010-2014 (n=3734).
finding: Modern Taiwanese women (2010-2014) who achieved vaginal delivery without adverse neonatal outcomes experienced significantly longer second stage labors than women 25 years ago (1991-1995), with birth weight, maternal age at delivery, and time period being significant associated factors.
birth_weight: Birth weight was identified as a significant factor associated with the duration of second stage labor for included normal neonatal outcomes, but no specific weight range was provided.
